title: Kahana vs Mighty Networks: A Room That Survives the Thread
excerpt: Mighty Networks is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. Kahana is the shelf and reading list beside the chat, not another inbox.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: Founded in 2011; headquartered in Palo Alto, CA.
2024 estimated revenue ≈USD 8.6M ARR (up from USD 6.8M in 2023); total funding ≈USD 66M; ~133 employees as of 2026.
Claims more USD 1M communities than any other platform, emphasis on monetized communities.
Pricing (2025–2026): Launch ≈USD 79/month; Scale ≈USD 215/month; Mighty Pro custom for branded apps; platform fees ~2%/1%/0.5%.

strengths.title: Beginner-friendly and community-rich
strengths.detail: Helps creators grow online communities quickly; more community features than many competitors.

strengths.title: Multiple monetization options
strengths.detail: Memberships, courses, paid events, bundles, and branded apps via Mighty Pro.

strengths.title: Integrated courses and content
strengths.detail: Community, courses, events, and subscriptions in one place, supports cohort-based experiences.

strengths.title: Branded mobile app potential
strengths.detail: Mighty Pro offers fully branded (white-label) apps, a unique advantage for larger brands.

weaknesses.title: Limited high-end course features
weaknesses.detail: Weaker than dedicated LMS tools on complex assessments, SCORM, and certificates.

weaknesses.title: No native video hosting
weaknesses.detail: Requires external hosting (Vimeo, YouTube, etc.) and integrations.

weaknesses.title: Integration dependence
weaknesses.detail: Email, advanced analytics, and some payment flows often need external tools, a more complex stack.

weaknesses.title: No PayPal support
weaknesses.detail: Payments via Stripe; lack of PayPal is a limitation for some creators.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Mighty Networks is real-time chat, groups, and community velocity. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Mighty is where creators, entrepreneurs, and brands build digital communities with cultural software.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Mighty Networks side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Mighty Networks you can use Courses, Memberships, Community & Messaging, and Storefronts as first-class product jobs. The job is hanging out, announcements, and live conversation, not packaging knowledge into something strangers can browse later.

Using Kahana with Mighty Networks

You can use both. Mighty Networks keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep live conversation on Mighty Networks. Pin a Kahana hub or Club link in a channel, discuss live there, and assign the next ebook, video, or course from Kahana so the syllabus is not buried in the thread.
